subject: arabic
license: Our own (story text written for Waymark)

data.title: The Stranger at the Gate
data.intro: Dust on your boots, the sun going down behind you. The caravanserai’s gate stands open, and lamplight spills across the courtyard. Over the arch, words are painted that you can’t read. The innkeeper, a broad woman with flour on her sleeves, looks you over. “You can’t read the signs on the road? Then sit. Every traveler starts with a few letters.”

trial.name: The Painted Sign
trial.text: The innkeeper hands you the sign from over the arch. Read 30 words from all your letters at 90% or better, and she’ll write your name in her book.

data.outro: You read it aloud, every word. The innkeeper writes your name in her book, in Arabic, and turns it so you can read that too. “ضيف,” she says. “Guest. Your cup is filled first now.”

data.text: The innkeeper taps the table: بيت. “House. You’re in one. Now you can say so.” The first milestone on the road catches the light.
A boy runs past with a sack of rice. رز, he shouts, and grins when you read it off the sack.
An old man by the fountain taps his wrist. “دم,” he says: blood. “Family is written there first.”
Two merchants argue over شاي. You read the word on the tin before they do. One of them laughs and pours you a glass.
The kitchen door opens: جاج on the board tonight. The cook calls something from deep in the throat, a ح that no Hebrew letter quite holds. You try it. She nods: almost.
A traveler from the south says ق like a g, a man from the hills like a k, the innkeeper not at all. “Three ways, one letter,” she shrugs. “Listen to who’s talking.”
The heavy letters. The storyteller makes them sound like a door closing. A merchant counts his coins: صفر, zero. A pilgrim sighs: سفر, the road. One heavy letter apart, and now you hear it.
The last milestone. The innkeeper takes down the painted sign over the arch and hands it to you. “Read it.”

data.title: The Carter’s Greeting
data.intro: A cart rattles in through the gate, and its driver jumps down before it stops. Salim greets the innkeeper, the cook, the boy with the rice and then you, twice each. “مرحبا! Hello! You’re the new guest? Sit with me. On the road, a greeting opens more doors than a key.”
milestones: Salim taps his chest, then yours. “Me, you. That’s half of every conversation.” He orders tea for both of you.
You thank the cook without thinking, and she answers before you can blush. Salim laughs into his tea.
Salim stands and greets a stranger at the gate, then waves you over to do the next one yourself. You do.

trial.name: The Carter’s Roll Call
trial.text: Salim greets the whole courtyard and wants you to keep up. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Salim claps you on the back. “You greet like you were born on this road.” From now on, his cup sits next to yours at the innkeeper’s table.

data.title: The Grandmother’s Questions
data.intro: An old woman in an embroidered dress takes the cushion across from you and studies you over her glasses. “Who are you? Where are you from? Who are your people?” This is Umm Khalil, and she won’t stop asking until she knows.
milestones: You ask Umm Khalil a question back. She raises an eyebrow, then smiles: “Good. Now you’re talking.”
Umm Khalil names her grandchildren, all of them, and checks that you can name your own family back.
A traveler asks where the well is. Before Umm Khalil can answer, you do.

trial.name: Umm Khalil’s Questions
trial.text: Umm Khalil has one more round of questions, and she expects answers. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: “Now I know who you are,” Umm Khalil says, and pats your hand. Her cushion stays across from yours at the table.

data.title: The Clockmender’s Count
data.intro: A thin man spreads a cloth on the table and lays out tiny gears in rows. Yusuf mends clocks, and he counts everything: steps, coins, minutes until supper. “One, two, three. Count with me, or you’ll lose your place.”
milestones: Yusuf hands you a gear and asks how many teeth it has. You count them in Arabic, out loud.
The courtyard clock strikes, and Yusuf asks you the time. You get it right before the last chime.
Yusuf plans his week out loud, day by day, and lets you finish the list.

trial.name: The Clockmender’s Count
trial.text: Yusuf sets his clocks running and starts counting. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Every clock Yusuf mended chimes at once. “You kept time,” he says. His cloth of gears stays on the corner of the table.

data.title: The Baker’s Daughter
data.intro: The smell reaches the table before she does: Rana, the baker’s daughter, with a basket of warm bread on her hip. “You’ve been eating here for weeks and you still point at things. Tonight you ask for them.”
milestones: You ask Rana for bread by name. She hands you the warmest piece in the basket.
Rana reads you the kitchen’s board and quizzes you on it. You name most of the dishes.
You order a whole supper, from soup to tea, and Rana writes it down without a single point.

trial.name: Rana’s Bread Basket
trial.text: Rana sets a full supper on the table, and you have to name it all. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Rana tears the last loaf in two and gives you half. “You eat like family now.” Her basket has a place at the table.

data.title: The Mason’s Plan
data.intro: A big man with plaster dust in his beard unrolls a drawing across the table: a house, room by room. Abu Fadi is building it for his son. “Help me with the words, guest. A house is nothing but its rooms.”
milestones: Abu Fadi points at the drawing, and you name the room. He marks it with a stub of pencil.
You walk the inn with Abu Fadi, naming doors, windows and stairs as you go.
Abu Fadi shows you where the furniture will stand, and you say where each piece goes.

trial.name: The Mason’s Plan
trial.text: Abu Fadi walks you through the finished drawing, room by room. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Abu Fadi rolls up the plan and writes your name on the corner. “Every house needs a guest.” His plans stay on the table.

data.title: The Guide at the Gate
data.intro: A wiry man in a dusty kufiya sits down with a map and a cup of coffee. Nasser leads travelers through the hills and the towns beyond. “You can’t stay in the courtyard forever. Out there, you need to ask the way.”
milestones: Nasser traces a road on the map, and you call out left, right and straight on.
You ask Nasser how to get to the market. He makes you ask twice, the second time faster.
Nasser plans a whole journey with you: the bus, the road, the station at the end.

trial.name: The Guide’s Map
trial.text: Nasser hands you the map and lets you lead. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Nasser folds the map and tucks it into your bag. “Now you can find your way back.” His coffee cup stays on the table.

data.title: The Painter’s Portrait
data.intro: A young woman sets up a small easel by the lamp and squints at you. Leila paints portraits for travelers to send home. “Sit still. And tell me what I’m painting: your eyes, your hair, the color of your coat.”
milestones: You name the colors on Leila’s palette, one by one, as she mixes them.
Leila paints your hands and asks you to name each part as she goes.
You describe the innkeeper to Leila, and she paints her from your words alone.

trial.name: Leila’s Portrait
trial.text: Leila finishes your portrait and asks you to describe it back to her. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Leila turns the easel around: it’s you, at the innkeeper’s table, mid-word. She hangs it over the table, where it stays.

data.title: The Spice Seller’s Scales
data.intro: A man with a brass scale and a dozen little sacks takes the end of the table. Hassan sells spices, and he never gives a price without a smile and a story. “You want za‘tar? First you bargain.”
milestones: You ask Hassan the price of cumin, and he names it. You make an offer back.
Hassan counts out your change slowly, testing you. You catch his mistake, and he laughs.
You buy for the whole inn: spices, coffee, sugar, and you pay what it’s worth.

trial.name: The Spice Seller’s Scales
trial.text: Hassan sets out his whole stall and dares you to buy it right. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Hassan weighs out a little bag of za‘tar and won’t take your coins. “For a friend.” His scale stays at the end of the table.

data.title: The Teacher’s Lesson
data.intro: A woman with a stack of exercise books sits down to mark them by the lamp. Miss Huda teaches the village children, and she asks about your work, your days and your plans. “Everyone here does something. What do you do?”
milestones: You tell Miss Huda what you do, and she corrects one word, kindly.
Miss Huda lets you mark a child’s homework. You find both mistakes.
You describe your whole working day to Miss Huda, from waking up to closing the door.

trial.name: Miss Huda’s Lesson
trial.text: Miss Huda gives you the lesson she gives her best class. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Miss Huda writes “excellent” on your page in red ink, in Arabic. Her stack of books stays on the table.

data.title: The Poet’s Evening
data.intro: An old man with a walking stick takes the cushion nearest the lamp. Jamil was a shepherd, and now he makes poems about the weather and the heart. “Tell me how the day was. Not the work: the sky, and how you felt.”
milestones: You tell Jamil it’s hot today, and he answers with a line about the sun.
Jamil asks what you love and what you can’t stand. You answer him in Arabic.
You tell Jamil about a happy day and a sad one, and he listens to both.

trial.name: The Poet’s Evening
trial.text: Jamil recites, and you answer him line by line. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Jamil closes his eyes and nods. “You speak from the heart now.” The whole table is full: every regular in their place, and you among them.

data.title: The Tailor’s Fitting
data.intro: Just when the table seemed full, the gate opens again: a caravan from the coast, its people dusty and loud. First down is Samira, a tailor with pins in her collar and a tape measure around her neck. She looks at your shirt and sighs. “Who sewed this? Sit. Tell me what you wear, and in what colors.”
milestones: You name the color of Samira’s scarf, and she holds up three more to test you.
Samira points at your boots, your belt and your bag in turn. You name each one before she can.
You tell Samira your shirt is dirty, and she laughs. “Clean, then. Wash it, and I’ll mend the sleeve.”

trial.name: Samira’s Fitting
trial.text: Samira measures you from shoulder to shoe, saying each word as she goes. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Samira pins a new collar on your old shirt. “Now you look like you live here.” She keeps a chair for you by her sewing basket.

data.title: The Grandfather’s Family
data.intro: An old man arrives with what seems like half the caravan behind him: sons, daughters, cousins and a baby asleep on someone’s shoulder. Abu Sami sits, and they all find a place around him. “My family,” he says. “Learn their names, and how each one is mine.”
milestones: Abu Sami points to his brother’s son and his wife’s sister. You say which uncle and which aunt each one is.
The baby wakes and grabs your finger. Abu Sami tells you who it belongs to, and you follow every word.
You tell Abu Sami about your own family and your friends at home. He listens, and remembers them all.

trial.name: Abu Sami’s Family Tree
trial.text: Abu Sami calls out each of his family in turn, and you say who they are. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Abu Sami puts the baby in your arms for a moment. “There. Now you’re family too.” His grandchildren wave to you every morning.

data.title: The Apprentice’s Kitchen
data.intro: A thin boy with a sack of onions follows the caravan’s cook into the kitchen. Karim is learning to cook, and he talks about food the whole time he chops. “Breakfast, lunch, dinner. Tell me what you want, and I’ll bring it.”
milestones: You order tea with no sugar, and Karim brings it with a grin and a plate of bread and butter.
Karim asks you to name the fruit in his basket. You get every one, even the grapes.
You tell Karim his soup is tasty, then that it’s a little sour. He tastes it and agrees.

trial.name: Karim’s Menu
trial.text: Karim brings dish after dish and asks what each one is. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Karim writes your name on the kitchen wall, next to the cook’s. “Our best customer.” He saves you the last piece of cake.

data.title: The New House
data.intro: A young woman with a key on a string sits down, tired and happy. Mona has just rented a house at the edge of the village, and it’s empty. “I need a lamp, a mirror, pillows, everything. Help me make a list?”
milestones: You and Mona walk through her house, and you name each room as you go in.
Mona asks where the lamp should go. You tell her: on the wall, upstairs, by the bookcase.
You help Mona make tea in her new kitchen, then close the windows and turn off the lights.

trial.name: Mona’s Housewarming
trial.text: Mona shows the whole table around her house, and you name everything in it. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Mona gives you a spare key on its own string. “Come for coffee whenever you like.” The house has a picture on the wall now, and it’s yours.

data.title: The Student’s Notebook
data.intro: A young man in glasses sits with a pile of books and doesn’t look up. Tariq is home from college and has a test in a week. “English, French, a little German. And Arabic grammar, which is the hardest. Will you study with me?”
milestones: You and Tariq trade words: his English for your Arabic. He writes yours in his notebook.
Tariq asks you to repeat a sentence slowly. You do, and he understands every word.
You answer all of Tariq’s homework questions out loud, and he checks them against the book.

trial.name: Tariq’s Exam
trial.text: Tariq gives you the test he’s been studying for. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Tariq passes his test, and says it’s half yours. He gives you his old dictionary, with your name inside the cover.

data.title: The Post Rider
data.intro: A woman on a bicycle rides straight through the gate with a bag of letters. Dalia carries the mail between the villages and she knows everyone’s news. “Letters, newspapers, and now phones that never stop. Help me sort this, will you?”
milestones: Dalia reads you an address on an envelope, and you find the right house for her.
Dalia’s phone rings, and she hands it to you. You answer it, and take the message.
You read Dalia the newspaper’s headlines while she fixes her bicycle.

trial.name: Dalia’s Mailbag
trial.text: Dalia empties her bag on the table and you sort the letters with her. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Dalia gives you the first letter ever addressed to you here, care of the innkeeper. Inside: a card from Salim, with a drawing of his cart.

data.title: The Musician’s Night
data.intro: When the lamps are lit, a man with an oud on his back sits near the fire. Fares plays at weddings in every town on the road. “Music, dancing, games: that’s what a free evening is for. What do you do for fun?”
milestones: Fares plays a song and asks you to name it. You can’t, but you can tell him you like it.
You tell Fares about a game you play at home, and he teaches you one in return.
Fares stops in the middle of a song and you sing the next line. The table cheers.

trial.name: Fares’s Song
trial.text: Fares plays all evening, and you keep up with every song. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Fares writes a verse about the traveler who learned to sing in Arabic. He plays it every time you walk in.

data.title: The Road to Amman
data.intro: A woman in a driver’s cap comes in, shaking dust from her coat. Amal drives the bus from the border to Amman and back, and she has seen every road between. “Where are you going next? Tell me, and I’ll tell you the way.”
milestones: Amal shows you the bus ticket and asks what each line says. You read her the whole thing.
You tell Amal which way Jordan is, and Lebanon, and Egypt. She nods at each one.
Amal asks about your journey here, from the day you set off. You tell it to her in Arabic.

trial.name: Amal’s Timetable
trial.text: Amal reads out the bus timetable and every stop on the road. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Amal gives you a ticket with no date on it. “For when you’re ready to see more.” It goes in your pocket, next to Mona’s key.

data.title: The Shepherd’s Hillside
data.intro: A boy comes in at dusk smelling of goats and grass. Ziad keeps his family’s flock on the hills above the village, and he knows every animal by name. “Come up with me tomorrow. I’ll show you the mountain, the lake and all my goats.”
milestones: On the hillside, Ziad points at birds, a donkey and a camel on the road. You name them all.
Ziad asks which season you like best. You tell him spring, when the wind is warm.
At night, Ziad shows you the moon and the stars over the desert, and you name them with him.

trial.name: Ziad’s Flock
trial.text: Ziad brings his flock down the mountain, and you name every animal that passes. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Ziad gives you a little bell from his best goat. “So the hills know you.” You hear it ring every time you walk in the courtyard.

data.title: The Merchant’s Ledger
data.intro: The caravan’s owner comes in last, with a heavy book under his arm. Abu Nabil counts everything: sacks, coins, days, miles. “A merchant who can’t count in Arabic gets cheated twice a week. Sit, and check my sums.”
milestones: Abu Nabil reads out the price of a sack in thousands, and you write it down right the first time.
You tell Abu Nabil which day the caravan leaves: Tuesday, at noon. He writes it in his book.
You add up a whole page of Abu Nabil’s ledger, and you find the mistake he left in to test you.

trial.name: Abu Nabil’s Accounts
trial.text: Abu Nabil reads out a month of accounts, and you check every number. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Abu Nabil closes the ledger. “You count better than my sons.” He writes your name in it, with a line all to yourself.

data.title: The Traveler from Baghdad
data.intro: A second caravan comes in from the east, bigger than the first, with tents rolled on the camels’ backs. Khalid has crossed every Arab country selling carpets, and he has a cousin in each. “Syrian, Iraqi, Yemeni, Moroccan: every one of them speaks Arabic, and none of them speaks it the same. Where are you from?”
milestones: Khalid names a city, and you name the country it’s in. He tries ten, and you miss one.
Khalid’s cousin from Tunis sits down, and you greet him with the word for where he’s from.
You tell Khalid where each of his carpets was made, from the pattern and his hints.

trial.name: Khalid’s Carpets
trial.text: Khalid unrolls a carpet from every country he has crossed, and you name them all. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Khalid gives you a small carpet from Iraq. “For your room. So you can say you’ve been somewhere.”

data.title: The Sailor’s Stories
data.intro: A man with a sea-captain’s beard and a sailor’s rolling walk takes a seat. Elias has sailed from Haifa to every port in Europe, and he tells it all at once. “France, Spain, Italy, Greece. I’ve been everywhere the sea goes. Ask me anything.”
milestones: Elias draws the sea on the table with his finger, and you name the countries along its shore.
Elias tells you the language each port speaks. You tell him which ones you’ve heard of.
You tell Elias where you’d sail first. He nods: a good choice, though cold in winter.

trial.name: The Captain’s Map
trial.text: Elias unrolls his old sea chart, and you name every country on it. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Elias gives you a brass compass. “So you always know which way home is, and which way the sea is.”

data.title: The Far Side of the Map
data.intro: A woman with three cameras around her neck sits down and orders tea in careful Arabic. Mei is from Taiwan, and she has photographed markets in forty countries. “I learned Arabic the way you are learning it. Look at my pictures, and tell me where they are.”
milestones: Mei shows you a market in India and one in Turkey. You tell her which is which.
You and Mei trade words for countries: her Chinese for your Arabic.
Mei asks which continent you’d visit first. You tell her, and why, in Arabic.

trial.name: Mei’s Album
trial.text: Mei shows you her whole album, one country a page. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Mei takes your picture at the innkeeper’s table, with every regular in it. She sends a copy with Dalia’s next mail.

data.title: The Surveyor’s Chain
data.intro: A man in a pressed shirt comes in with a long measuring chain and a book of numbers. Rami measures the new road the caravans will use. “Kilometers, kilograms, thousands of stones. And the work must be done before September.”
milestones: Rami reads you a distance in kilometers, and you write it down in numbers without a pause.
You tell Rami which month the rains start. He moves his plan back a month.
You check Rami’s count of the stones for the road: five thousand, three hundred. He was right.

trial.name: The Surveyor’s Count
trial.text: Rami reads out a page of measures and months, and you check every one. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Rami names a milestone on the new road after the traveler who checked his numbers. It’s your name, carved in Arabic.

data.title: The Market Stall
data.intro: A woman with a cart of clothes sets up beside the gate and comes in for her lunch. Nour sells shirts, jeans and coats in the market, and she never lets a customer pay too much. “Small, medium, large. Cash or card. Come and try it, and I’ll tell you the price.”
milestones: You ask Nour the price of a coat, and pay in cash. She gives you the right change.
Nour holds up a shirt and asks if it’s your size. You tell her you need a large.
You ask the waiter for the bill for Nour’s lunch and yours, and pay it before she can.

trial.name: Nour’s Bargain
trial.text: Nour sells her whole cart in an afternoon, and you help with every sale. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Nour gives you a belt from her cart. “No charge. You brought me three customers today.”

data.title: The Doctor’s Rounds
data.intro: A doctor with a leather bag comes in from the village late at night. Nadia visits the sick in all the villages around, and she eats whatever the innkeeper puts in front of her. “Eat well, sleep well, and you won’t need me. Now, who here is ill?”
milestones: You tell Nadia that the cook has a headache. She gives you the medicine to take to her.
Nadia asks what you ate today. You tell her, and she says it’s too much ice cream.
You help Nadia at the hospital for a morning, and tell her what each patient says.

trial.name: The Doctor’s Questions
trial.text: Nadia asks you everything she asks a patient. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Nadia writes you a prescription: “Rest one day a week.” The innkeeper pins it on the wall.

data.title: The Holiday Crowd
data.intro: A big man in a bright shirt comes in with a guitar and a phone full of pictures. Antoine went to Brazil forty years ago and has come home for a holiday. “Music, dancing, swimming, and a selfie with everyone! A day out isn’t a day out without it.”
milestones: Antoine shows you pictures from Mexico and Chile, and you name each country.
You buy tickets for the whole table to a concert in town. Antoine pays for the ice cream.
Antoine takes a selfie with you at the pool, and you tell him to send it to everyone.

trial.name: Antoine’s Day Out
trial.text: Antoine plans a day out for the whole table, and you plan it with him. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Antoine leaves you his guitar when he flies home. “Play for Fares. Tell him the song is from Brazil.”

data.title: The Old Friend’s Words
data.intro: The first regular you met comes back through the gate with his cart. Salim has been on the road for a season, and he talks faster than ever. “You know the words. Now learn the other words: the ones people use when they’re not being careful.”
milestones: Salim says “okay” three different ways, and you answer each one the right way.
Salim asks why, when and how many, and you answer before he finishes the question.
You tell Salim what you think about the road, and he says you sound like a local.

trial.name: Salim’s Return
trial.text: Salim talks the way he talks to his oldest friends, and you keep up. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Salim laughs. “Now you even argue like us.” He sits back in his old seat, next to yours.

data.title: The Barber’s Chair
data.intro: A barber sets up his chair under the arches every Friday, and today he comes in for tea. Abu Hani shaves the whole village and hears everyone’s news. “A beard, a mustache, a cut. Sit, and tell me about your week, from waking up to falling asleep.”
milestones: Abu Hani asks how you slept. You tell him: badly, and you dreamed of camels.
You sneeze in the barber’s chair, and Abu Hani tells you what to say. You say it.
Abu Hani shaves you, and you describe your whole day to him without stopping.

trial.name: The Barber’s Gossip
trial.text: Abu Hani tells you the whole village’s news, from head to toe. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Abu Hani gives you a free shave every Friday from now on. “A regular’s right.”

data.title: The Spice Road
data.intro: The second caravan’s cook comes into the kitchen and argues with the innkeeper about salt. Umm Ali cooks for forty travelers a day, and she tastes everything. “Salty, sweet, bitter, spicy. A cook needs a tongue first and hands second.”
milestones: Umm Ali gives you a spoon of everything on the stove, and you say how each one tastes.
You buy garlic, eggplant and chickpeas in the market for Umm Ali, with nothing forgotten.
Umm Ali asks how to cook the falafel: fried or baked. You tell her, and she agrees.

trial.name: Umm Ali’s Kitchen
trial.text: Umm Ali cooks a whole dinner, and you name every dish and taste. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Umm Ali teaches you her falafel. You make it for the whole table, and nobody leaves any.

data.title: The Builder’s House
data.intro: Abu Fadi the mason comes back, and his son is with him. They’re building a house in the village with a basement, three floors and an elevator, the first in the valley. “Come and see it. Tell me what goes in each room.”
milestones: Abu Fadi’s son shows you the stairs, from the basement to the roof. You name every floor.
You tell Abu Fadi where the stove, the freezer and the kettle go in the kitchen.
Abu Fadi asks where you’d put the curtains and the carpet. You tell him, and he writes it down.

trial.name: The New House’s Rooms
trial.text: Abu Fadi walks you through the finished house, room by room. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Abu Fadi gives you the key to the roof. “The best view in the valley. Come up whenever you like.”

data.title: The Hiring Fair
data.intro: A woman with a list sits down and starts asking everyone what they do. Wafa runs the new factory in town and needs workers. “Engineers, mechanics, a nurse, a cook. And someone who can talk to all of them.”
milestones: Wafa asks you what each regular does for work. You tell her, and she writes them down.
You help Wafa write a notice: the working hours, the salary and when the breaks are.
Wafa holds a meeting with her new workers, and you explain each job in Arabic.

trial.name: Wafa’s Interviews
trial.text: Wafa interviews twenty workers, and you help with every one. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Wafa offers you a job. You say no, kindly, in Arabic. She laughs and says the offer stays open.

data.title: The Long Way Round
data.intro: Amal the bus driver comes back with news: the new road is open, and she drives to the coast and the border now. “Bus, ship, plane: I’ve booked them all for travelers. Now you can go abroad and back, if you know how to ask.”
milestones: Amal asks where to park the bus in town. You tell her: by the square, at the corner.
You change money with Amal for her next trip, and count it twice.
Amal tells you how to check in at the airport. You tell it back to her, step by step.

trial.name: Amal’s New Route
trial.text: Amal drives you along the whole new road, from the square to the border. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: Amal stamps the ticket she gave you long ago. It’s good for anywhere now, whenever you’re ready.

data.title: The Innkeeper’s Story
data.intro: On the quietest night of the year, the innkeeper sits down at her own table for the first time. She pours two cups, one for you. “Everyone has told you their story. Mine is short. Do you want to hear it?”
milestones: The innkeeper tells you about the year she came here, long ago. You listen without asking for a single word.
She asks what you’re afraid of and what you hope for. You tell her both, in Arabic.
She asks what you’ll do one day, when you leave. You tell her your plan, and she says it’s a good one.

trial.name: The Innkeeper’s Night
trial.text: The innkeeper asks you everything, the way a friend does. Hear and read 30 of the chapter’s words at 90% or better.

data.outro: The innkeeper turns her book to the first page. Under “guest,” she has written a new word next to your name: صاحب. Friend of the house.
